registration.method: phase correlation on locally normalised bedrock windows; RANSAC affine; held-out validation

nasa_reference.statement: NASA: blinking the June 30, 2007 and Oct. 13, 2007 HiRISE images, registered on fixed bedrock features, shows ripple motion on a dark sand dune over 105 days; site near 8.7 N, 67.3 E. Scale bar 85 m.

also.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/International Research School of Planetary Sciences

regions.explanation: Most of the region lies on bright bedrock, which should not move; the difference is more likely lighting or residual misregistration.

regions.explanation: A texture difference survives registration, masking and noise filtering on dark dune sand, but no independent published observation covers this exact spot. Ripple migration is the likely explanation, yet the 14.7 degree change in solar incidence angle between the two images can also alter how ripples look.

regions.explanation: The region lies on the dune shown in NASA's PIA15680 before/after pair, where NASA documented ripple movement over the 105-day interval. Our pipeline found the difference independently, and the NASA frame was located in both HiRISE products by template matching (scores 0.92 / 0.93).
